NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the critical nexus of AI infrastructure, designing high-performance GPUs and accelerators that are fabless-manufactured almost exclusively through TSMC using advanced nodes, creating a concentrated upstream dependency on TSMC and HBM memory suppliers like SK Hynix. Downstream, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily driven by hyperscalers and cloud providers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) racing to build out AI training and inference capacity, making NVIDIA both a critical enabler and a key beneficiary of the global AI infrastructure buildout.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly sophisticated global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer of proprietary silicon and a master systems integrator that sources specialized components from a concentrated set of Asian and Western suppliers, most critically TSMC for chip fabrication. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily through its own direct channels (retail stores, apple.com) and carrier/retail partners to hundreds of millions of end consumers, while also monetizing its installed base through high-margin services revenue from developers, advertisers, and platform partners.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC sits at the critical nexus of the global semiconductor supply chain, acting as the world's dominant pure-play foundry that transforms designs from fabless chip companies into physical silicon using cutting-edge manufacturing processes. It is heavily dependent on a concentrated group of Western equipment suppliers (particularly ASML for irreplaceable EUV tools) for capital inputs, while serving as an essential — and often sole-source — manufacturing partner for the world's most valuable technology companies including Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain as one of only three major DRAM manufacturers (alongside Samsung and SK Hynix), making it critically dependent on a concentrated set of semiconductor capital equipment suppliers for its highly capital-intensive fab operations. On the demand side, Micron serves a broad but increasingly AI-driven customer base, with surging HBM demand from hyperscalers and GPU makers representing its highest-growth and highest-margin opportunity, while traditional PC, mobile, and enterprise markets provide volume scale.

IREN.supply_chain_summary: IREN operates at the intersection of Bitcoin mining and AI-focused data center infrastructure, making it critically dependent on NVIDIA GPU supply and low-cost electricity procurement to drive both mining economics and high-performance compute revenue. On the downstream side, IREN's revenue is bifurcated between Bitcoin liquidation through crypto exchanges (principally Coinbase) and emerging AI/HPC cloud compute contracts with hyperscale and enterprise customers, exposing the company to both crypto market volatility and the rapidly growing demand for GPU compute capacity.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at the intersection of the nuclear fuel supply chain and next-generation clean power generation, depending critically on a very limited set of HALEU fuel suppliers and specialized nuclear component manufacturers to build and operate its Aurora microreactors. On the demand side, Oklo targets high-growth, power-hungry customers such as hyperscale data center operators and energy-intensive industrial users who require reliable, carbon-free baseload electricity, though the company remains pre-revenue and most downstream relationships are in letter-of-intent or early contracting stages.
